candidates.name: Practice guide 41: developing estates - registration services
verified_facts: The site survey normally forms the basis of estate boundary and layout plans.
Land surveyors are expected to monitor development and record changes to the original layout, including as-built plans where appropriate.
Unreported layout changes can cause HM Land Registry to withdraw estate-plan approval.
semantic_limits: An approved or historic layout must not be assumed to match current physical geometry after site changes; current evidence and lineage are required.

candidates.name: Return and rejection of applications for registration (practice guide 49)
verified_facts: HMLR requires plans to show actual scale and orientation and sufficient detail for identification on Ordnance Survey mapping.
Undefined boundaries should be shown accurately and where necessary by measurements.
Plans marked for identification only or with unsuitable scale treatment may not satisfy registration requirements.
semantic_limits: A plan that fails HMLR clarity/scale requirements is not promoted into high-confidence geometry evidence for parcel matching or height attribution.
